item.title: Pleasanton council to consider Asset Management Plan, raise for city manager
item.description: The Pleasanton City Council will hear an update Tuesday on the progress to create the city’s first-ever Asset Management Plan. A 3% raise for the city manager and city attorney, the railroad quiet zone project and grants for Tri-Valley Haven’s shelter are among consent highlights. The post Pleasanton council to consider Asset Management Plan, raise for city manager appeared first on Pleasanton Weekly.

item.title: Ignoring transfer rules has forever changed high school athletics – and at what cost?
item.description: “It’s caused a crisis of consciousness for me many times. But instead of giving up, I look for the good stories on homegrown athletes and hope that a miracle can happen to restore character to high school athletes. item.title: ShopConsciously offers ethically sourced, unique gifts at Pleasanton’s first self-serve store
item.description: If you’ve ever walked down Main Street in downtown Pleasanton, chances are you’ve passed by ShopConsciously, an artisanal gift store that sells ethically sourced products such as bags made from recycled bottles by women in Kenya, Africa. item.title: EBRPD expands future parkland with 190-acre acquisition
item.description: East Bay Parks has announced that it added about 190 acres of new parkland next to Thurgood Marshall Regional Park, Home of the Port Chicago 50, strengthening open space protection and future park connectivity in eastern Contra Costa County. item.title: Pleasanton Preps: Amador boys’ soccer posts wins at all three levels
item.description: The Amador Valley boys’ soccer program saw wins for all three levels last week. The varsity got an early goal from Jonas Lyions off an assist from Matthew Sun, then the Amador defense made the goal stand up as the team earned the 1-0 win. item.title: Vehicle falls off tow truck, ends up on BART tracks in Castro Valley
item.description: A vehicle fell off of a tow truck and onto BART train tracks in Castro Valley following a crash on Interstate Highway 580 on Tuesday afternoon, snarling traffic for commuters on the highway and stopping train service for hours. item.title: Gulf Gas Station signage debate comes to an end following council approval last month
item.description: The contentious debate over new signage at the Gulf Gas Station on the corner of First Street and Vineyard Avenue came to a close last month after the Pleasanton City Council approved the latest modifications made to the gas station’s canopy and monument sign.
